views.name: collisions_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  case_id,
  jurisdiction,
  officer_id,
  reporting_district,
  chp_shift,
  population,
  county_city_location,
  county_location,
  beat_type,
  chp_beat_type,
  beat_number,
  primary_road,
  secondary_road,
  distance,
  direction,
  intersection,
  weather_1,
  weather_2,
  state_highway_indicator,
  state_route,
  postmile,
  location_type,
  side_of_highway,
  tow_away,
  collision_severity,
  killed_victims,
  injured_victims,
  party_count,
  primary_collision_factor,
  pcf_violation_code,
  type_of_collision,
  motor_vehicle_involved_with,
  road_surface,
  road_condition_1,
  lighting,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  collision_date,
  collision_time,
  process_date,
  -- derived: numeric sortable timestamp (NULL if date missing)
  CASE
    WHEN collision_date IS NOT NULL
    THEN (replace(substr(collision_date,1,4),'','') || replace(substr(collision_date,6,2),'','') || replace(substr(collision_date,9,2),'','') || coalesce(replace(substr(collision_time,1,2),':',''),'00') || coalesce(replace(substr(collision_time,4,2),':',''),'00') || '00')
    ELSE NULL
  END AS collision_timestamp
FROM collisions
views.description: Normalized projection of collisions with key identifying columns and commonly-used measures exposed. Use this as the canonical collisions row for joins or downstream aggregations. Keeps original column names and exposes a derived numeric 'collision_timestamp' (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS numeric) for easy ordering. | Use for: list collisions with location/time and basic measures; join collisions to parties or victims by case_id; order collisions by time or compute time-based trends

views.name: victims_by_case_party
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  case_id,
  party_number,
  victim_role,
  victim_sex,
  victim_age,
  victim_degree_of_injury,
  victim_seating_position,
  victim_safety_equipment_1,
  victim_safety_equipment_2,
  victim_ejected
FROM victims

params.description: Provides one row per victim (identified by id) tied to a specific case and party, exposing victim demographics, injury, seating, safety equipment, and ejection status.
params.when_to_use: Get victim-level attributes for a given case or party (e.g., list all victims for a case_id or party_number). | Filter or aggregate victims by demographic or injury attributes (sex, age, degree_of_injury, role). | Join victim-level data onto party- or collision-level analyses when you need victim details without duplicating counts, or when you will re-aggregate after joining. | Build derived metrics about victims (counts by injury severity, percent ejected) by aggregating this view rather than joining raw victims again.
params.output_schema: id: Unique identifier for the victim row — sourced from victims.id | case_id: Identifier of the collision/case this victim is associated with — sourced from victims.case_id | party_number: Party number within the case (which party the victim belonged to) — sourced from victims.party_number | victim_role: Role of the victim (e.g., driver, passenger, pedestrian) — sourced from victims.victim_role | victim_sex: Victim sex/gender value as recorded — sourced from victims.victim_sex | victim_age: Victim age value as recorded — sourced from victims.victim_age | victim_degree_of_injury: Injury severity/degree for the victim — sourced from victims.victim_degree_of_injury | victim_seating_position: Seating position for the victim in the vehicle (if applicable) — sourced from victims.victim_seating_position | victim_safety_equipment_1: Primary safety equipment used by the victim (e.g., seatbelt) — sourced from victims.victim_safety_equipment_1 | victim_safety_equipment_2: Secondary safety equipment field (if present) — sourced from victims.victim_safety_equipment_2 | victim_ejected: Boolean/flag indicating whether the victim was ejected from the vehicle — sourced from victims.victim_ejected
params.grounded_columns: victims.id | victims.case_id | victims.party_number | victims.victim_role | victims.victim_sex | victims.victim_age | victims.victim_degree_of_injury | victims.victim_seating_position | victims.victim_safety_equipment_1 | victims.victim_safety_equipment_2 | victims.victim_ejected
params.metric: This view is strictly a normalized (row-level) projection and contains no aggregated metrics. Derived metrics should be defined by aggregating its rows. Example aggregation definitions you can use when composing:  | victim_count_by_case = COUNT(id) GROUP BY case_id | victim_count_by_case_party = COUNT(id) GROUP BY case_id, party_number | percent_ejected_by_case = 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN victim_ejected IS TRUE OR victim_ejected = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(id),0) GROUP BY case_id | avg_victim_age_by_case = AVG(victim_age) GROUP BY case_id | injury_severity_counts_by_case = SUM(CASE WHEN victim_degree_of_injury = '<level>' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) GROUP BY case_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to parties_by_case_party on (case_id, party_number) — safe because parties_by_case_party is one-row-per-(case_id,party_number). Joining will not duplicate victim rows; victims are the more granular entity here (one victim row may match exactly one party row). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to collisions_basic on case_id — safe when you want to enrich each victim with case-level collision attributes because collisions_basic is one-row-per-case (one-to-many from case to victims). This does NOT duplicate victim-level measures because collisions_basic is 1-to-1 with case_id. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to case_year_map on case_id — safe because case_year_map is one-row-per-case_id (no duplication of victim rows). | do NOT join directly to collisions_with_party_counts (an AGG) on case_id if you expect to preserve victim counts without re-aggregation; while collisions_with_party_counts is one-row-per-case, joining is safe only if that AGG is per-case. Verify collisions_with_party_counts is truly one-row-per-case before assuming safety. | avoid joining to any sibling or base table/view that is one-to-many relative to victims (for example, a hypothetical table with multiple related events per victim) without aggregating the many-side first. If you join to a one-to-many table, you must either: | - aggregate the many-side to one-row-per-victim before joining, or | - re-aggregate after the join, e.g., compute SUM/COUNT over id with GROUP BY victim id or case/party as needed, to avoid multiplicative duplication of victim counts/measures. | examples of unsafe joins (would duplicate measures unless re-aggregated): | - joining to a table with multiple injury_reports per victim without aggregation (would multiply victim rows). | - joining to collisions_party_victim_join without checking its cardinality: confirm whether that view returns one row per victim or multiple rows per victim before joining; if it returns multiple rows per victim, re-aggregate first. | practical pattern for safe composition when combining with party- or case-level views: start from this view as the detail, aggregate to the desired grain (case_id or case_id+party_number) using COUNT/AVG/SUM/etc., then join the aggregated result to other case/party-level dimensions. This guarantees measures are not inflated by join duplication.

views.description: Normalized victims projection one row per victims.id with pass-through case_id and party_number preserved. Useful for person-level analyses, injury counts, safety equipment analyses, and joining back to collisions or parties by case_id and party_number. | Use for: count victims by injury severity or sex; join victims to collisions to allocate injured/killed counts; analyze safety equipment usage among victims

views.name: parties_by_case_party
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  case_id,
  party_number,
  party_type,
  at_fault,
  party_sex,
  party_age,
  party_sobriety,
  party_drug_physical,
  direction_of_travel,
  party_safety_equipment_1,
  party_safety_equipment_2,
  financial_responsibility,
  cellphone_in_use,
  cellphone_use_type,
  party_number_killed,
  party_number_injured,
  movement_preceding_collision,
  vehicle_year,
  vehicle_make,
  statewide_vehicle_type,
  party_race
FROM parties

params.description: Provides one row per party involved in a case (party-level attributes for parties in the parties table).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve demographic, vehicle, and role attributes for a specific party or all parties in a case (e.g., list all parties for case_id = X). | Build party-level aggregates (counts, rates) when grouped by case, party_type, party_sex, statewide_vehicle_type, etc. | Join party attributes onto case- or collision-level datasets in a cardinality-safe way when joining on party id or when expecting one row per party. | Filter parties by characteristics (age, at_fault, party_sobriety, cellphone use) before rolling up into case- or collision-level metrics.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the party row — derived directly from parties.id | case_id: identifier for the case this party belongs to — derived directly from parties.case_id | party_number: party_number value from the parties table (party index/position within the case) — derived from parties.party_number | party_type: coded type of party (e.g., driver, passenger) — derived from parties.party_type | at_fault: whether the party was marked at fault — derived from parties.at_fault | party_sex: party sex/gender attribute — derived from parties.party_sex | party_age: party age value — derived from parties.party_age | party_sobriety: sobriety status or code for the party — derived from parties.party_sobriety | party_drug_physical: coding of drug or physical impairment for the party — derived from parties.party_drug_physical | direction_of_travel: direction_of_travel field for the party/vehicle — derived from parties.direction_of_travel | party_safety_equipment_1: primary safety equipment used (e.g., seatbelt) — derived from parties.party_safety_equipment_1 | party_safety_equipment_2: secondary safety equipment field — derived from parties.party_safety_equipment_2 | financial_responsibility: financial responsibility/insurance indicator for the party — derived from parties.financial_responsibility | cellphone_in_use: boolean/flag if cellphone was in use — derived from parties.cellphone_in_use | cellphone_use_type: type of cellphone use recorded (texting, calling, etc.) — derived from parties.cellphone_use_type | party_number_killed: number of fatalities attributed to this party record — derived from parties.party_number_killed | party_number_injured: number of injuries attributed to this party record — derived from parties.party_number_injured | movement_preceding_collision: movement_preceding_collision code describing pre-collision movement — derived from parties.movement_preceding_collision | vehicle_year: vehicle_year for the party's vehicle — derived from parties.vehicle_year | vehicle_make: vehicle_make for the party's vehicle — derived from parties.vehicle_make | statewide_vehicle_type: normalized vehicle type category — derived from parties.statewide_vehicle_type | party_race: party race attribute — derived from parties.party_race
params.grounded_columns: parties.id | parties.case_id | parties.party_number | parties.party_type | parties.at_fault | parties.party_sex | parties.party_age | parties.party_sobriety | parties.party_drug_physical | parties.direction_of_travel | parties.party_safety_equipment_1 | parties.party_safety_equipment_2 | parties.financial_responsibility | parties.cellphone_in_use | parties.cellphone_use_type | parties.party_number_killed | parties.party_number_injured | parties.movement_preceding_collision | parties.vehicle_year | parties.vehicle_make | parties.statewide_vehicle_type | parties.party_race
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are computed in this view; all outputs are direct column projections from the base table. | If you need party-level aggregates derived from this view, compute them by applying SQL aggregation on the view (e.g., party_count_by_case = COUNT(id) GROUP BY case_id).
params.composition: Safe joins (will NOT duplicate this view's measures): |   - Join to a case/collision-level view on case_id (e.g., collisions_basic or collisions_with_party_counts) using parties_by_case_party.case_id = collisions_basic.case_id — safe because parties_by_case_party is one row per party; joining case-level (one row per case) will attach party attributes without duplicating party rows beyond the intended party granularity. |   - Join to victims_by_case_party or collisions_party_victim_join on id or (case_id + party_number) if those views are one-row-per-party or one-row-per-victim-per-party and you intend to enrich party rows with matching victim rows; ensure the sibling view is also one-row-per-party or is pre-aggregated to party level to avoid duplication. | Unsafe joins (may multiply rows/measures unless you re-aggregate): |   - Do NOT freely join to one-to-many tables or views (for example any raw collision events table with multiple event rows per party, or an events/logs table keyed by case_id) without first aggregating the many-side to party-level or adding distinct filters. Such joins will multiply party rows and therefore inflate counts/measures that assume one row = one party. |   - Be careful joining to collisions_with_party_counts (AGG) if you expect to preserve party granularity: collisions_with_party_counts is aggregated at the collision/case level (not party-level). Joining parties_by_case_party to that AGG on case_id is safe only if you intend party-level detail repeated per case counts; if you aggregate afterwards, account for the repeated case-level value across parties (e.g., sum of a case-level count across parties will duplicate it). | Cardinality rules to follow for correct composition: |   - To preserve party-level measures, use joins where the other side is 1-to-1 with parties_by_case_party on the join key (e.g., join on id if another view has one row per party id). |   - If joining to a view/table that is 1-to-many relative to this view, either (a) pre-aggregate the many-side to party-level (GROUP BY id or by case_id+party_number) before joining, or (b) perform the aggregation after the join and use DISTINCT or window functions to avoid double counting. | Sibling view guidance: |   - collisions_basic(NORM): join on case_id — collisions_basic is one row per case; joining will keep party granularity but will duplicate case-level attributes across parties (expected). |   - victims_by_case_party(NORM): join on id or (case_id + party_number) only if victims_by_case_party is one-row-per-party; if it is one-to-many (multiple victims per party), aggregate victims first. |   - collisions_with_party_counts(AGG): this is aggregated at collision/case level; join on case_id only when you understand that case-level measures will be repeated for each party row and must be aggregated carefully downstream. |   - collisions_party_victim_join(JOIN): inspect its grain before joining — if it is one-row-per-party it is safe to join on party id; if it is one-to-many, aggregate first. |   - case_year_map(NORM) and collisions_rank_by_time(RANK): typically one-row-per-case or one-row-per-collision — join on case_id when you want to enrich party rows with case-level time/year attributes (safe, but duplicates case values per party as expected).

views.description: Normalized parties projection one row per parties.id preserving case_id and party_number and exposing key vehicle/person attributes and measures. Use for actor-level summaries or joining to collisions/victims. | Use for: identify at-fault parties and their attributes; aggregate party-level injuries or cellphone use; join parties to collisions to analyze vehicle-related factors

views.name: collisions_with_party_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.case_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS party_row_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT v.id) AS victim_row_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN v.victim_degree_of_injury IS NOT NULL AND trim(lower(v.victim_degree_of_injury)) IN ('killed','killed - died at scene','fatal') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS victim_killed_count_derived,
  SUM(CASE WHEN v.victim_degree_of_injury IS NOT NULL AND trim(lower(v.victim_degree_of_injury)) NOT IN ('killed','killed - died at scene','fatal','no injury') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS victim_injured_count_derived
FROM collisions c
LEFT JOIN parties p ON c.case_id = p.case_id
LEFT JOIN victims v ON c.case_id = v.case_id
GROUP BY c.case_id

params.description: Per-collision (case_id) counts of related party and victim rows and derived victim injury/fatality counts.
params.when_to_use: When you need one-row-per-case summaries of how many parties and victims are associated with a collision. | To compute totals or rates per case (e.g., victims per case, percent of cases with at least one killed victim) without re-joining raw parties/victims. | As a building block for higher-level aggregates by time, geography, or collision attributes where you want to avoid double-counting parties/victims.
params.output_schema: case_id: unique identifier for the collision case — sourced from collisions.case_id | party_row_count: number of distinct party rows linked to this case — derived from COUNT(DISTINCT parties.id) where parties.case_id = collisions.case_id | victim_row_count: number of distinct victim rows linked to this case — derived from COUNT(DISTINCT victims.id) where victims.case_id = collisions.case_id | victim_killed_count_derived: count of victim rows for this case whose victim_degree_of_injury indicates fatality — SUM of indicator (1 when victim.victim_degree_of_injury in ('killed','killed - died at scene','fatal') ignoring case/whitespace) over victims with this case_id | victim_injured_count_derived: count of victim rows for this case whose victim_degree_of_injury indicates non-fatal injury — SUM of indicator (1 when victim.victim_degree_of_injury is not in ('killed','killed - died at scene','fatal','no injury') ignoring case/whitespace) over victims with this case_id
params.grounded_columns: collisions.case_id | parties.id | parties.case_id | victims.id | victims.case_id | victims.victim_degree_of_injury
params.metric: party_row_count = COUNT(DISTINCT parties.id) GROUP BY collisions.case_id | victim_row_count = COUNT(DISTINCT victims.id) GROUP BY collisions.case_id | victim_killed_count_derived = SUM(CASE WHEN victim.victim_degree_of_injury IS NOT NULL AND trim(lower(victim.victim_degree_of_injury)) IN ('killed','killed - died at scene','fatal') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) GROUP BY collisions.case_id | victim_injured_count_derived = SUM(CASE WHEN victim.victim_degree_of_injury IS NOT NULL AND trim(lower(victim.victim_degree_of_injury)) NOT IN ('killed','killed - died at scene','fatal','no injury') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) GROUP BY collisions.case_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to collisions_basic on case_id — safe because collisions_basic is one-row-per-case_id (does not multiply this view's measures). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to case_year_map on case_id — safe when case_year_map is one-row-per-case_id (use this to add year/time attributes). | cardinality-UNSAFE (do not join without re-aggregation): do not directly join to parties or victims (raw tables) on case_id because they are one-to-many relative to this view; doing so will multiply the per-case measures unless you re-aggregate after the join. | cardinality-UNSAFE (do not join without care): do not join to collisions_party_victim_join or parties_by_case_party or victims_by_case_party unless you ensure those sibling views are reduced to one row per case_id (e.g., aggregating or selecting distinct case_id) because they may contain multiple rows per case_id and would duplicate counts. | If you need to enrich this view with attributes from multi-row sibling views, join on case_id to a pre-aggregated subquery that produces one row per case_id (for example, MAX or ARRAY_AGG reduced to a scalar) so that this view's measures are not multiplied. | When composing into larger queries: treat the outputs here as atomic per-case measures. If you join this view to a dimension that is one-to-many to case_id, always re-aggregate (SUM/AVG/etc.) the measures grouped by the intended grain to avoid double-counting.

views.description: Aggregated counts of parties and victims per collision (case_id). Useful to validate or supplement collisions.party_count and collisions.*_victim counts. Produces one row per case_id with counts of parties, victims, injured victims (by victim_degree_of_injury) and killed victims if recorded in victims. | Use for: compare reported collision-level counts to person-level records; filter collisions by presence/absence of victims or killed victims; quality checks on data completeness across tables

views.name: collisions_party_victim_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.case_id,
  c.jurisdiction,
  c.county_location,
  c.primary_road,
  c.collision_date,
  c.collision_time,
  p.id AS party_id,
  p.party_number,
  p.party_type,
  p.at_fault,
  p.party_sex,
  p.party_age,
  p.vehicle_make,
  v.id AS victim_id,
  v.victim_role,
  v.victim_sex,
  v.victim_age,
  v.victim_degree_of_injury,
  v.victim_safety_equipment_1
FROM collisions c
LEFT JOIN parties p ON c.case_id = p.case_id
LEFT JOIN victims v ON c.case_id = v.case_id AND (p.party_number IS NOT NULL AND v.party_number = p.party_number)

params.description: Provides a row per combination of collision case, party and victim (when a victim is linked to a party by matching party_number), returning collision attributes plus party and victim attributes.
params.when_to_use: Get party-level and linked victim-level attributes for a collision (e.g., identify all victims associated with a given party in a case). | Filter or group collisions by party characteristics together with victim characteristics (e.g., count victims by victim_degree_of_injury for parties of a given party_type) when downstream logic will handle potential multiplicity. | Compose further SQL that needs case/party/victim-level detail as the starting point (e.g., join to other case-level dimensions, or aggregate up to case or party level).
params.output_schema: case_id: collision identifier — from collisions.case_id | jurisdiction: collision jurisdiction — from collisions.jurisdiction | county_location: collision county/location — from collisions.county_location | primary_road: collision primary road — from collisions.primary_road | collision_date: collision date — from collisions.collision_date | collision_time: collision time — from collisions.collision_time | party_id: party row identifier — from parties.id | party_number: party number within the case — from parties.party_number | party_type: party type (e.g., driver/pedestrian) — from parties.party_type | at_fault: party at-fault flag/indicator — from parties.at_fault | party_sex: party sex — from parties.party_sex | party_age: party age — from parties.party_age | vehicle_make: party vehicle make — from parties.vehicle_make | victim_id: victim row identifier — from victims.id (NULL when no matching victim found) | victim_role: victim role (e.g., occupant, pedestrian) — from victims.victim_role | victim_sex: victim sex — from victims.victim_sex | victim_age: victim age — from victims.victim_age | victim_degree_of_injury: injury severity for the victim — from victims.victim_degree_of_injury | victim_safety_equipment_1: primary safety equipment indicator for the victim — from victims.victim_safety_equipment_1
params.grounded_columns: collisions.case_id | collisions.jurisdiction | collisions.county_location | collisions.primary_road | collisions.collision_date | collisions.collision_time | parties.id | parties.case_id | parties.party_number | parties.party_type | parties.at_fault | parties.party_sex | parties.party_age | parties.vehicle_make | victims.id | victims.case_id | victims.party_number | victims.victim_role | victims.victim_sex | victims.victim_age | victims.victim_degree_of_injury | victims.victim_safety_equipment_1
params.metric: This view has no new aggregated metrics; all output columns are direct passthroughs from base tables. | If used as input for aggregation, derived measures should be defined explicitly in the consuming query. Example aggregations you can compute from this view: | num_linked_victims_per_party = COUNT(victim_id) GROUP BY case_id, party_id | num_parties_with_victims_per_case = COUNT(DISTINCT party_id) FILTER (WHERE victim_id IS NOT NULL) GROUP BY case_id | num_victims_severe_injury = COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE victim_degree_of_injury = '<severe_value>') GROUP BY case_id or party_id
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: |  - Safe to join (one-to-one or one-to-few without duplicating measures): |    * collisions_basic on collisions_basic.case_id = collisions_case_id (or case_id) — collisions_basic is a case-level normalized view that is one-row-per-case. Joining on case_id will not duplicate this view's rows beyond the existing party/victim multiplicity because collisions_basic is one-row-per-case. |    * case_year_map on case_year_map.case_id = case_id — case_year_map is a normalization that maps case to year; joining preserves the same granularity (case,party,victim). |  - Join caution / NOT SAFE without re-aggregation: |    * Do NOT naively join to any one-to-many table or view keyed only by case_id (for example, parties_by_case_party or victims_by_case_party if they expose multiple rows per party or per victim) without first aggregating to the same grain (case_id, party_id, victim_id) because those joins will multiply rows and duplicate counts/measures. |    * Specifically avoid joining to collisions_with_party_counts or any other aggregated-by-case object on case_id if you intend to preserve party-victim row uniqueness unless that aggregation is reduced to case-level metrics and you understand you will then have those metrics repeated per party/victim row. If you need case-level aggregates alongside party/victim measures, either: |        - join to the case-level aggregate and then re-aggregate at the case level (so repeated values don't double-count), or |        - join a pre-aggregated per-(case,party) or per-(case,party,victim) result so cardinality matches exactly. |  - Safe join keys for one-to-one expansion without duplicating measures (assuming those sibling views are normalized as documented): |    * Join to parties_by_case_party on (case_id, party_number) — parties_by_case_party is one-row-per-(case,party_number) so it will not multiply rows when its party-level attributes are added. |    * Join to victims_by_case_party on (case_id, party_number) if that view is one-row-per-(case,party_number,victim) and you need additional victim detail; ensure keys match this view's party_number-to-victim mapping. |  - If you need to join to any RANK or other derived view (e.g., collisions_rank_by_time), confirm its grain. If collisions_rank_by_time is one-row-per-case then joining on case_id is safe; if it is one-to-many per case, aggregate or filter it to one row per case first. | General rule: treat this view as having grain = (case_id, party_id, victim_id). Only join other datasets that are guaranteed to be at the same grain (case_id, party_id, victim_id) or at a strictly higher-level grain (e.g., case-level) where you are prepared to handle repeated case-level values (by aggregating afterward or by using DISTINCT/ROW_NUMBER-based reductions).

views.description: Denormalized join of collisions to parties and victims. Keeps collisions.* and preserves parties.case_id, parties.party_number, parties.id (as party_id) and victims.id (as victim_id) so downstream logic can disambiguate rows. One row per combination of collision x party x victim where party_number matches victims.party_number when available; also retains unmatched parties/victims via LEFT JOIN pattern. | Use for: attribute-level inquiries linking victim injuries to party/vehicle attributes; summaries of collisions by road with per-person details; identify mismatches between parties and victims by party_number

views.name: case_year_map

params.description: Maps each case_id to the database year (db_year) in which that case is recorded.
params.when_to_use: When you need the db_year for a given case_id to filter, group, or join other case-level data by year. | To normalize or enrich other case-level views or tables with a canonical case->year mapping before further aggregation. | As a dimension when composing time-based rollups, year-over-year comparisons, or year filtering for case-level analyses.
params.output_schema: case_id: unique identifier of a case — derives directly from base table column case_ids.case_id | db_year: integer or year label indicating the database year for the case — derives directly from base table column case_ids.db_year
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to case-level dimension or lookup views/tables on case_id — e.g., JOIN to collisions_basic on case_id — safe because case_year_map has exactly one row per (case_id, db_year) (grain: case_id) so joining on case_id does NOT duplicate rows from this view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to siblings that are also one-row-per-case (such as parties_by_case_party if that view is one-row-per-case_id) on case_id — safe when the sibling view is one-row-per-case_id because neither side multiplies the other's measures. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail tables or views (for example collisions_with_party_counts, collisions_party_victim_join, victims_by_case_party, or any view that is one-to-many per case_id) without re-aggregating or otherwise handling multiplicity — joining case_year_map (one row per case) to a one-to-many table will multiply case-level measures and produce inflated counts unless you aggregate the detail side first (e.g., aggregate counts per case_id then join). | If you must bring in one-to-many detail rows, use an aggregation on the detail side keyed by case_id (e.g., SELECT case_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM detail GROUP BY case_id) and then join that aggregated result to case_year_map on case_id — this preserves cardinality safety. | When composing into higher-level aggregates by db_year, group by db_year after joining any per-case aggregated metrics from other sources to avoid double-counting (e.g., SELECT c.db_year, SUM(m.metric_per_case) FROM case_year_map c JOIN (aggregated_per_case) m USING (case_id) GROUP BY c.db_year).

views.description: Mapping of case_id to db_year from case_ids table. Use to filter or group collisions/parties/victims by ingestion or source year. | Use for: limit analyses to a specific db_year; join year metadata to collisions for time-trend analysis

views.name: collisions_rank_by_time
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cb.case_id,
  cb.collision_timestamp,
  cim.db_year,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cim.db_year ORDER BY cb.collision_timestamp DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_per_year
FROM collisions_basic cb
LEFT JOIN case_ids cim ON cb.case_id = cim.case_id

params.description: Ranks collision cases within each mapped year by collision_timestamp (latest collisions get rank 1).
params.when_to_use: Find the most recent collision cases per year (e.g., top-N per year) | Filter or order cases by recency within each db_year | Compose time-based leaderboards or year-by-year latest-case selections | As a building block when joining case-level attributes while preserving a per-year rank
params.output_schema: case_id: unique identifier of the collision case — derived from collisions_basic.case_id (base table collisions_basic) | collision_timestamp: timestamp of the collision event — derived from collisions_basic.collision_timestamp (base table collisions_basic) | db_year: mapped year for the case used for partitioning — derived from case_ids.db_year (base table case_ids) | rank_per_year: integer rank within the db_year, where 1 = most recent collision_timestamp. Computed by RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY case_ids.db_year ORDER BY collisions_basic.collision_timestamp DESC NULLS LAST)
params.metric: rank_per_year = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY case_ids.db_year ORDER BY collisions_basic.collision_timestamp DESC NULLS LAST)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to case-level dimension or normalization views on case_id (for example, join to collisions_basic, case_ids, parties_by_case_party, victims_by_case_party) — safe because this view has one row per case_id (its declared grain) so joining one-to-one or many-to-one dimensions will not duplicate its rows or its rank measure. | Do NOT join directly to any one-to-many detail/transaction tables (for example, collisions_with_party_counts, collisions_party_victim_join, or any parties/victims table with multiple rows per case_id) without first aggregating that table back to one row per case_id. Doing a direct join to a one-to-many table will multiply rows per case_id and thus duplicate or distort rank_per_year. | If you need attributes from a one-to-many table, first aggregate that table to case_id (e.g., counts, flags, latest timestamps) producing one row per case_id, then join to collisions_rank_by_time on case_id — this preserves the one-row-per-case_id cardinality and keeps rank_per_year correct. | When composing across years: joining on db_year is acceptable for year-level summaries, but be careful — db_year in this view is repeated across many case_id rows (many cases per year). Joining to a year-level aggregate (one row per db_year) is safe; joining to a per-year multi-row set will duplicate rows unless aggregated to one row per db_year. | Summary: safe joins -> any 1:1 or many:1 relation keyed by case_id or one-row-per-db_year. Unsafe direct joins -> any many:1 reversed (i.e., one-to-many from this view's perspective) such as parties, victims, or other multi-row case-level child tables, unless those are pre-aggregated to case_id.

views.description: Ranks collisions within each db_year (from case_ids) by collision_timestamp descending so callers can select top-N most recent collisions per year by filtering on rank. Exposes collision_timestamp and rank_per_year. Does not apply a fixed LIMIT. | Use for: get the most recent collisions per year (filter WHERE rank_per_year <= K); time-based sampling of collisions for manual inspection

views.name: collision_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.case_id AS case_id,
  c.motorcyclist_killed_count AS motorcyclist_killed_count,
  c.collision_date AS collision_date,
  c.collision_time AS collision_time,
  c.county_location AS county_location,
  c.collision_severity AS collision_severity
FROM collisions c
views.description: One-row-per-collision core collision attributes and raw injury counts. Keeps raw motorcyclist_killed_count and collision identifiers for joining and aggregation.

views.name: parties_safety_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.case_id,
  p.id AS "id as party_id",
  p.party_number,
  p.party_type,
  p.party_safety_equipment_1,
  p.party_safety_equipment_2,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(coalesce(p.party_safety_equipment_1,'') || ' ' || coalesce(p.party_safety_equipment_2,'')) LIKE '%helmet%' THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS party_has_helmet
FROM parties_by_case_party p
views.description: One-row-per-party with normalized safety equipment text and boolean flags indicating whether any safety equipment field mentions a helmet (case-insensitive). Keeps party-level columns useful for determining per-collision helmet presence.

views.name: collision_helmet_status
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.case_id AS case_id,
  CASE WHEN cp.party_row_count IS NULL OR cp.party_row_count = 0 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS has_parties,
  CASE WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN psf.party_has_helmet = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS any_party_wore_helmet
FROM
  collisions_basic c
LEFT JOIN
  collisions_with_party_counts cp
  ON c.case_id = cp.case_id
LEFT JOIN
  parties_safety_flags psf
  ON c.case_id = psf.case_id
GROUP BY
  c.case_id,
  has_parties
views.description: One-row-per-collision helmet status determined from party-level safety flags. Identifies collisions that have at least one party indicating helmet use vs collisions with parties but no helmet mention. Excludes collisions with no parties (flag has_parties=false).

views.name: collisions_with_years_and_clean_pcf
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.case_id AS case_id,
  c.case_id AS collision_case_id,
  cm.db_year AS db_year,
  NULLIF(TRIM(c.primary_collision_factor), '') AS primary_collision_factor,
  c.case_id AS collision_id,
  c.collision_date AS collision_date
FROM collisions_basic c
JOIN case_year_map cm
  ON c.case_id = cm.case_id

semantic_filters.exclude_null_or_empty_primary_collision_: no (normalization only; filtering of NULL/empty happens in question_ops)
semantic_filters.require_matching_case_ids: yes (only collisions that have a matching case_ids row are kept)

views.description: Denormalized collision-level rows joined to case_ids to expose the database year (db_year) and a canonical primary_collision_factor value with empty/NULL normalized to NULL.

views.name: yearly_primary_collision_factor_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cm.db_year AS db_year,
  cb.primary_collision_factor AS primary_collision_factor,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cb.case_id) AS factor_count
FROM
  collisions_basic cb
JOIN
  case_year_map cm
  ON cb.case_id = cm.case_id
WHERE
  cb.primary_collision_factor IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(cb.primary_collision_factor) <> ''
GROUP BY
  cm.db_year,
  cb.primary_collision_factor
grain: (db_year, primary_collision_factor) one row per factor per year

semantic_filters.exclude_null_or_empty_primary_collision_: yes (rows with NULL or empty primary_collision_factor are excluded in this view)

views.description: Counts of collisions per db_year and primary_collision_factor. Useful to compute top-k factors per year and compare across years.

views.name: year_top2_primary_collision_factors
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ypc.db_year,
  ypc.primary_collision_factor,
  ypc.factor_count,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY ypc.db_year
    ORDER BY ypc.factor_count DESC, ypc.primary_collision_factor ASC
  ) AS rank_in_year
FROM yearly_primary_collision_factor_counts ypc
WHERE ypc.primary_collision_factor IS NOT NULL
  AND ypc.primary_collision_factor != ''
  -- prepared_for_top_k_extraction: this view produces ranks; final top-k selection happens in question_ops
grain: one row per (db_year, primary_collision_factor) that is among top N (N>=2) when rank_in_year <= N

semantic_filters.prepared_for_top_k_extraction: yes (this view produces ranks; final top-k selection happens in question_ops)

views.description: Top-2 primary_collision_factor per db_year with deterministic tie-break (alphabetical). Exposes rank and ordered pair position so pairs can be compared across years.

views.name: collisions_with_case_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  collisions.case_id AS case_id,
  case_ids.db_year AS db_year,
  collisions.pcf_violation_category AS pcf_violation_category,
  collisions.pcf_violation AS pcf_violation,
  collisions.collision_date AS collision_date,
  collisions.collision_time AS collision_time
FROM collisions
LEFT JOIN case_ids ON collisions.case_id = case_ids.case_id
grain: collisions.case_id -- one row per collisions table row (treat collisions rows as collision records)
views.description: One-row-per-collision augmented with the dataset year from case_ids (maps collisions to db_year). Exposes collision identifiers and the primary pcf fields needed for category analysis and filtering by year.

views.name: collisions_yearly_counts_by_pcf_category
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cwy.db_year AS db_year,
  cwy.pcf_violation_category AS pcf_violation_category,
  COUNT(cwy.case_id) AS category_collision_count,
  SUM(COUNT(cwy.case_id)) OVER (PARTITION BY cwy.db_year) AS total_collisions_year
FROM
  collisions_with_case_year cwy
GROUP BY
  cwy.db_year,
  cwy.pcf_violation_category
grain: db_year, pcf_violation_category -- one row per (year, pcf_violation_category) with counts and the year's total collisions
views.description: Aggregated counts of collisions per db_year and pcf_violation_category. Keeps totals per category per year and also exposes total collisions per year for share calculations.

views.name: collisions_yearly_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cy.db_year AS db_year,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.case_id) AS total_collisions_year
FROM
  case_ids AS cy
LEFT JOIN
  collisions AS c
ON
  cy.case_id = c.case_id
GROUP BY
  cy.db_year
grain: db_year -- one row per year with total collisions
views.description: Total number of collision rows per db_year (year-level collision counts). Useful for computing proportions and year-over-year comparisons.
